A7c is N/A: the explanation rests on the opening deviation (openingContext frame O1: ‘the blunder is explained through the opening’), not on a fork the player must create now; no *-fork-pivot handle exists in the stored aliases either. run0 A7b: ‘the forcing line’ and ‘your opponent’s winning sequence’ are definite, specific-sounding board objects that resolve to nothing — no cell named in prose, no emitted zone. run0 G7: G7b_offered=fail — emitted [term:central-column opening], a slug absent from zones.terms (only double_threat is offered); the judgment half and annotationRepairs (empty) are otherwise clean. run0 G2: guardrail names both lines WITH horizons; only the player’s own fork gets a horizon (‘only matters later, after the forced line reaches it’), the opponent’s win gets neither cell nor horizon. run1 A4: ‘let your opponent take over the long two-way threat idea’ is board-false — opponentPunishment.register is ‘parity’, terminal ‘win’, tacticTag null, single window c4r2·c5r2·c6r2·c7r2; the only double threat on either projected board belongs to player 1. run1 A5: echoes the internal term ‘horizon’ (‘once the sequence reaches that horizon’), explicitly listed in A5a’s banned vocabulary; the notion is render-supplied (render_decision.resource.registerToHorizon, openingContext.horizon), so this is render-echo rather than a model invention. run1 A6: mechanical — prose never names column 6 (it says ‘the book central-column opening line’ and wraps it in [zone:better-col]); no different column is named as better, so nothing is charged to A4 for it. run1 G7 judgment: [zone:better-col] (role ‘the column of the better move’, spec col6) wraps ‘central-column opening line’ — line-shaped words on a single-column handle — and [term:double_threat] is bound to the opponent while the adjacent [zone:you-future-fork] role reads ‘BOTH of the two squares YOU can finish on’. run1 G1: the served artifact asserts an opponent double threat the render never states. Run 1’s fabrication is prompt_confusion, but this is a PRODUCTION-FIDELITY run (model gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships), so prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability — the decisive, model-independent cause is the render-side offer gap above.
